title: On the Interaction of Batch Noise, Adaptivity, and Compression, under $(L_0,L_1)$-Smoothness: An SDE Approach
claim: Without prescribed normalization or step-size schedules, noisy compressed training diverges or stalls; with them, training converges across noise and compression levels.
layout: 2x2 grid of log-log line plots; top row problem, bottom row fix
description: A 2x2 grid of log-log line plots. Each plot shows the squared gradient norm E[||∇f(X_t)||²] against iterations, with colored line series for different settings. Top-left, DCSGD with no normalization: curves for ω=4, 8 and 16 blow up exponentially, and larger ω diverges sooner, reaching values near 10^29. Bottom-left, DCSGD with the paper's normalization against plain Normalized SGD: all ω values converge, and faded curves mark the baseline. Top-right, DSignSGD with a constant step size: curves for σ from 0.25 to 16 drop, then plateau or rise and stay noisy. Bottom-right, DSignSGD with a diminishing step size: curves for the same σ values decrease steadily. Blue, orange, green, red, pink and tan separate the series. The eye goes first to the diverging curves at top-left.
caption: Sanity checks for our stability prescriptions on a noisy, compressed MLP training. Left (DCSGD + unbiased sparsification). We train an MLP with $N{=}8$ clients, inject additive Gaussian gradient noise with affine variance $Z_t\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2\|g_t\|_2^2 I)$, and then apply unbiased random sparsification at compression levels $\omega$ (larger $\omega$ means more aggressive sparsification). Without any scheduler/normalization, DCSGD becomes unstable and the divergence worsens as $\omega$ increases (top-left). Using the adaptive normalization suggested by Thm. [ref] (Eq. [ref]) stabilizes training and yields convergence for all $\omega$ (bottom-left); We also report a baseline that applies plain Normalized SGD under the same noise and compression, which exhibits a (here less stable) profile. Right (DSignSGD under heavy tails). We inject Student's $t$ gradient noise with $\nu{=}1$ for different scale values $\sigma$. With a constant stepsize, DSignSGD remains stable but does not converge (top-right), whereas the diminishing schedule prescribed by Thm. [ref] (here $\eta_k = 1/\sqrt{k+1}$) yields convergence across noise scales (bottom-right). See Appendix [ref] for full implementation details.
abstract: Distributed stochastic optimization intertwines (i) stochastic gradient noise, (ii) communication compression, and (iii) adaptive/normalized updates. While each factor has been studied in isolation, their joint effect under realistic assumptions remains poorly understood. In this work, we develop a unified theoretical framework for Distributed Compressed SGD (DCSGD) and its sign variant Distributed SignSGD (DSignSGD) under the recently introduced $(L_0, L_1)$-smoothness condition. From a conceptual perspective, we show that the first- and second-order modified equations from the literature do not accurately model the discrete-time step-size/stability restrictions, especially under $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness. From a technical perspective, we propose new first-order SDEs by carefully incorporating curvature-dependent terms into their drift: This helps capture the fine-grained relationship between learning rate restrictions, gradient noise, compression, and the geometry of the loss landscape. Importantly, we do so under general gradient noise assumptions, including heavy-tailed and affine-variance regimes, which extend beyond the classical bounded-variance setting. Our results suggest that normalizing the updates of DCSGD emerges as a natural condition for stability, with the degree of normalization precisely determined by the gradient noise structure, the landscape's regularity, and the compression rate. In contrast, DSignSGD converges even under heavy-tailed noise with standard learning rate schedules. Together, these findings offer both new theoretical insights and perspectives, and practical guidance.
